title: Comparing with <, >, =
examples: Teacher, what does the symbol mean when numbers are the same?
Can you show me how to use the greater than sign?
If I have five apples and you have three, which symbol do I use?

explain.say: You can compare two numbers with a sign. The sign shows which number is bigger.
There are three signs: less than, greater than and equal to. The open side of the sign faces the bigger number.

draw.text: The open side faces the bigger number

explain.say: Compare four and seven. Seven is bigger, so the open side faces seven. You read it as four is less than seven.
Compare nine and two. Nine is bigger, so the open side faces nine. You read it as nine is greater than two.
When two numbers are the same, you use the equals sign. Five equals five.

faq.a: The sign < means less than. The number on the left is smaller. The point of the sign faces the smaller number.
asks: What does the less than sign mean?
When is a number less than another?

faq.q: How do I know which way the mouth opens?
faq.a: The open side always faces the bigger number. The point always faces the smaller number.
asks: Which way does the symbol face?
How do I tell which side is bigger?

faq.q: What does the equals sign mean?
faq.a: The equals sign means both sides have the same value or amount.

faq.q: Can I use <, >, or = for letters?
faq.a: No, we only use these symbols to compare numbers or amounts. They are for counting things, not for letters.
asks: Do I use these symbols for words?
Are these symbols for counting only?

faq.q: If I have three blocks and you have three blocks, what symbol do I use?
faq.a: You both have three blocks, so the numbers are the same. You use the equals sign: three equals three.
asks: What symbol shows they are the same?
How do I show they match?

facts: The greater than sign is written >.
The less than sign is written <.
The equals sign shows that two things are the same.
The open side of the sign always faces the bigger number.

quiz.say: Tap the sign that goes between 6 and 2.
quiz.why: Six is bigger than two. The open side faces six.

wrong.1: That says six is less than two, and six is bigger.
wrong.2: That says six and two are the same, and they are different.

quiz.say: Tap the sign that goes between 9 and 9.
quiz.why: Nine and nine are the same. The equals sign shows the same value.

wrong.0: That says nine is less than nine, and they are the same.
wrong.2: That says nine is greater than nine, and they are the same.

quiz.say: Tap the sign that goes between 3 and 8.
quiz.why: Eight is bigger than three. The open side faces eight.

wrong.0: That says three and eight are the same, and they are different.
wrong.1: That says three is greater than eight, and eight is bigger.
